entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production concept art for a buildable, high-detail interactive 3D desktop automaton in the Atomic Heart aesthetic.
Reference image: the supplied REST/READ board defines the original ceramic, gold and black-vinyl design language and the shared round pedestal. This request is a major refinement of the UPPER record-player, not a new pedestal.

Create one exceptionally polished, physically credible cinematic product render, front three-quarter camera, full object clearly framed at large size, dark charcoal studio background, subtle contact shadow. No collage, no UI or hovering labels, no typography outside the object.

The user rejects the current implementation as undersized, thin, toy-like, repetitive primitive geometry, and inadequate material quality. Make the record player a substantial intricate mechanical sculpture that occupies its pedestal confidently. Preserve the shared pedestal as the same shape and dimensions: 2.74 diameter and 0.670608 height, same ivory curved front fascia, nickel stepped rims, left curved selection hatch, power button at one end, ruby X close button at the other end. Between them only physical engraved controls: indexed number dial, modulation slider, pressure paddle, play/pause rocker, split service rocker. No detached UI panel. Do not make the pedestal taller, smaller, or change its layers to cheat proportions.

Redesign/refine the mechanism above it: six identical large black archive records with finely scalloped cast-gold rims and ivory numbered tabs in six separate ivory petal-shaped rear magazine slots. At this depicted reading state, FIVE records remain in rear slots and the sixth SAME-SIZE record is on the independent FRONT small turntable. The selected original slot is visibly empty. Rear magazine broad and substantial, nearly fills the rear width; records visibly large, not coins. Front turntable is approximately .90 diameter relative to the base 2.74, and record diameter .84, so it nearly fills the platter, leaving only a slender gold bearing rim. Absolutely no tiny disc on a broad blank turntable, no gigantic whole-pedestal record. The black disc remains under any future printed specimen.

A robust, sculptural two-link ivory-and-gold pickup arm rises from a broad cast ceramic rear shoulder. Thick tapered curving housings, recessed joint clevises, actual bolts, bearing races, separate cast brass yokes, red ceramic torque inserts, visible restrained cable conduits, three elegant articulated rim-gripping fingers. Arm parked back and high, making a readable articulated silhouette with negative spaces; it cannot occlude the specimen volume above the front platter. No skinny straight cylinders used as a whole arm, no disconnected jewelry. A separate sinuous reading tonearm on the right reaches the large record, its tiny amber optical point physically contacting a record groove. Only this tiny reading light in this render; VFX will be designed separately. Rear mechanism scale about 1.4 times the previous board's weak-looking upper structure, total upper silhouette feels roughly 2.3 wide and 2.0 tall above the unchanged base. Mechanical proportions coherent, all six media equal.

Materials: convincing warm ivory fired ceramic with silky clear glaze, gentle orange-peel only at microscopic scale, smooth rounded transitions and sharp controlled seams; absolutely no canvas weave, cardboard or plastic. Champagne gold and pale nickel are visibly different alloys, broad rich reflection gradients, turned/burnished contact surfaces, satin cast sections, restrained machining marks and crevice patina, polished bevel edges, no black grime wash and no uniform yellow flat color. Black vinyl stays deep black with fine radial grooves and soft reflection, not a silver mirrored disc. Ruby enamel restrained to controls and hubs.
Lighting: physically plausible large diffused warm key and cool narrow edge light, legible reflected studio cards, soft occlusion inside joints, balanced filmic highlights without clipping, razor-clean physically modelable details. High-end AAA hero prop/art department quality, not low-poly game icon, not cartoon, not an orthographic assembly of tori and cylinders. Prioritize form, construction, material hierarchy over indiscriminate detail noise.

entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production hero concept for a physical 3D interactive automaton in the art direction of Atomic Heart.
Input reference: only the ivory ceramic / champagne metal / black vinyl palette and SAME layered round pedestal. Replace the old upper gripper design completely with the new AI mechanism below. Do not preserve the claw.

A superb cinematic hard-surface hero prop render, one complete object on a charcoal studio background, large front three-quarter view. Sophisticated Soviet retrofuturist industrial robotics, witty and uncanny rather than children's toy. Warm ivory glazed ceramic, cast champagne brass, brushed pale nickel, black optical glass, disciplined ruby accents. Refined purposeful construction and beautiful studio reflections, physically plausible surface finishes and micro-machining, no rough canvas, no heavy grime, no primitive low-poly styling. No text outside the object, no diagram arrows, no HUD or floating user interface.

One shared circular pedestal, diameter 2.74 relative units, height .67, preserve its ivory curved front, stepped metal rings and physical control cassette. Do not alter these base proportions. Physical controls only: left power, six-number selector wheel, slider, broad pressure button, obvious play/stop rocker, split service rocker, red close X. Physical sculpted controls and enamel inlays integrated into the curved console.

Above the base: a substantial broad six-slot automatic archive-disc changer. Six IDENTICAL .84-diameter black discs, refined radial vinyl grooves, fine scalloped gold rim, small ivory numbered tabs. FIVE remain in separate sculptural ceramic storage petals at the rear. The sixth is HOVERING, rigid and horizontal, directly over the separate front .90-diameter turntable, with its original slot visibly empty. All six records must have the same world size, including the hovering record; no replacement jumbo record. The front small turntable diameter is ONE THIRD of the shared base diameter, and the hovering disc is 93 percent of this turntable diameter, leaving a slim rim when it lands. The rear magazine is broad, fills the rear part of the pedestal rather than looking like tiny coins on a large empty base. Clear pathways and substantial integrated ceramic castings.

A strong sculptural ivory two-link arm with recessed gold bearings and cable routing rises behind the magazine. At its END is a large SPHERICAL AI CAMERA HEAD, approximately .55 diameter (two-thirds of a record diameter), visibly attached through a real gold gimbal neck. NO gripper, NO claws, NO fingers anywhere. The head is the character of the object: a polished ivory segmented ball, black circular forward camera eye, a sophisticated ring of overlapping camera-iris metal shutter blades and amber 24x24 pixel matrix expression behind smoked lens glass. The expression is attentive and a little mischievous: two simple amber raised pixel eyes inside ONE circular lens, no cartoon human mouth, no emoji sticker, no floating face panel. Ruby side indicator, tiny service seams, bronze screws.

Its UNDERSIDE carries a separate compact gimballed magnetic-optical emitter, so the face can look at the viewer while the downward emitter stays aimed at the disc. The disc is held .18 units below the emitter by a SHORT, well-defined pale amber tractor field: narrow converging patterned rays, a restrained translucent volumetric core, thin moving interference rings on the disc surface. Visible air gap, no physical touching or tether. This is a sci-fi optical gripper, not a wide smoky spotlight. Show the head leaning slightly to inspect the floating disc above the front platter. Keep front face, hovering record and empty slot readable at once. A separate small sinuous right-side optical tonearm is parked out of the platter volume. No printed specimen yet; this picture establishes the new robot personality and larger consistent record proportions.

Modelable details: distinct head shell quarters, real iris leaves with overlap, lens barrel, pitch/yaw gimbal, independent underside emitter, indexed magazine cradles, large bearings, restrained fasteners with correct scale. Gold has structural mass, not thin gold outlines painted over white geometry. Thick sculptural shoulder and tapered arm links, no long skinny pipes. Soft broad reflections and controlled rim light reveal actual form. High-end AAA close-up prop quality and a coherent original design, not a collection of spheres and tori.

entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production VFX storyboard for the SAME Atomic Heart style ivory-and-gold AI archive player in the reference. Make a refined 2x2 four-keyframe art-direction sheet. Large legible panels, cinematic high-end game close-up rendering, charcoal background, coherent physical geometry across panels. Small unobtrusive panel labels only: "01 READ", "02 DRAW", "03 CAST", "04 ALIVE". No game UI, no hovering control panels, no fantasy runes.

Invariant mechanism: rear six-disc magazine with exactly five large black equal-size stored discs and one empty slot; sixth original disc stays FLAT on the separate front platter throughout all four frames. Record nearly fills its platter (93% diameter), platter one third of unchanged round base diameter. SAME .84-diameter disc in every state. The spherical ivory AI head has actual overlapping metal camera-iris blades and amber pixel eyes inside smoked black glass, on a substantial articulated ivory/gold arm, no claws. AI head and its underside emitter park off the specimen's volume once the disc has landed; they must never intersect the architecture being printed. All controls physically built into the unchanged pedestal.

Subject being constructed: a richly crafted original miniature CLOCKWORK OBSERVATORY, not a crude square building or flat hologram. An ivory curved split-shell clock tower with open arches, gold structural ribs, visible fine planetary gears behind a glass clock face, counterweights, slender curved stair, small orrery crown with ruby sun. It fits on the record, roughly one record diameter wide and 1.3 record diameters tall. Objects have real manufactured thickness, coherent shafts and bearings. Sculptural readable silhouette, details are modeled, no blobs or flat cards.

01 READ: original record on platter, right-hand curved optical tonearm reading its groove with a tight ruby/amber contact point. AI tilts its head and narrows real mechanical iris in concentration. Disc radial engraved lines wake in a short localized traveling pattern. Emitter glow stops at the solid disc surface; no light passes through the vinyl and no beam to the ground. No building yet, anticipatory energy restrained.

02 DRAW: tonearm PARKED clear. A recognizable three-dimensional blueprint of that exact observatory rises from the disc's own grooves: slender ice-blue structural ribs, architectural curves and clockwork outlines attached to their actual future positions; a few coherent warm-gold filaments stream from radial sectors of the record into the correct anchor points. This is an intricate dimensional construction loom, not a flat hologram plane, not a generic laser cylinder, not a cheap circular spell. Lower structure is becoming real gold while the upper ribs are fine pale-blue ghost geometry. Tiny luminous material flecks travel INTO assembly edges, not random fireworks in space. The head watches from outside the construction space.

03 CAST: the emotional peak. Real warm reflective gold skeleton at bottom, glazed ivory panels condensing and closing onto their precise supports, an intense but narrow WHITE-GOLD formation boundary climbing over the actual geometry. Retain the fine pale-blue incomplete architecture above the boundary and gold filament threads feeding its edges. A beautiful complex spiral of short layered trails close to the structure, real depth occlusion and localized illuminated surfaces. Density and intensity peak where pieces lock, not a large glowing ring covering the object. Rich spatial layers, controlled highlight cores, amber edge bloom, readable metal and ceramic even at climax. Fine warm sparklets are drawn to rivets and clockwork hubs and extinguish on contact. No generic smoke billboards.

04 ALIVE: exactly that observatory is fully opaque and physically substantial, matching its previous construction silhouette. Clock gears and pendulum start, ruby orrery sun lifts, record and observatory slowly rotate together on the same spindle. Construction scaffold and loose particles have fully disappeared. A restrained warm travelling glint remains in real gold grooves, practical light at the core. The AI turns to the viewer, tilts 8 degrees and performs a proud pixel-eye squint as its iris partly blinks. No persistent huge glow obscures the finished sculpture.

Materials and lighting: high-end fired porcelain glaze, champagne brass with broad rich specular gradients, satin nickel, deep black vinyl, restrained ruby enamel. Contrast from excellent film lighting and actual chamfered construction, no dirty uniform dark metal, no canvas texture, no plastic toy sheen. Maintain the machine, record size, specimen construction and camera across all panels. This is a buildable layered VFX target with clear contacts, occlusion, onset, climax and complete recovery.

entries.prompt:
Edit target: this reference image of the spherical AI record player. Preserve its full machine, camera, base, FIVE stored records, numbered cradles, arm construction, spherical iris head, materials and studio lighting. This is a precision edit to show the same object during printing.

CRITICAL GEOMETRY INVARIANT: Keep the front SMALL turntable exactly the same diameter and position it already has in the reference image (approximately one third of the base diameter). Keep the large annular metal deck around it entirely exposed as metal. Do NOT turn the whole base top black. The large deck is NOT a record and NOT a turntable. Do NOT enlarge the small turntable. The hovering record in the reference is moved DOWN onto this exact small turntable without changing its diameter; the record nearly fills that small turntable and is the same size as the five records in storage. Keep the five stored records the same size. A black disc covering the whole base is absolutely wrong.

The original hovering black record is now resting flush on the small platter, with its gold scalloped edge and slender exposed supporting metal rim. There is exactly ONE record on the small platter and NO duplicate floating record. Turn off the tractor beam completely. Move the AI head and its arm only slightly to the right and back, safely outside a volume directly over the small platter, watching attentively. Keep the independent right tonearm parked clear. Do not change the whole composition.

Above the SMALL platter, build a jewel-like architectural CLOCKWORK OBSERVATORY as a real tabletop miniature, not a giant tower. Its footprint is about .65 times the small platter diameter; its height is about 1.2 times the small platter diameter. Its crown stays below the top of the AI head. The miniature has actual glazed ivory curved shells, a gold arch framework, fine planetary gears visible in a glass clock face, an open spiral stair and ruby orrery crown. Hero-prop-grade manufactured detail, sophisticated Atomic Heart design language.

Depict the print crescendo beautifully with clear depth: bottom two-thirds is finished solid gold and ivory, upper third consists of the exact future thin architectural structural ribs in pale ice-blue luminous blueprint. Warm gold light filaments feed upwards from sectors of the SAME small black record into actual architectural junctions, with tiny coherent inward-flying material grains. A narrow white-gold moving formation edge follows the structure at two-thirds height, brighter around real joints, lighting the nearby ivory locally. No generic big magic ring, no random fireworks, no huge translucent cylinder. The broad metal deck around the SMALL platter stays visible and free of projection patterns except very faint natural reflected light. No printing effect anywhere on the stored records or base rim.

AI's mechanical iris is partly narrowed and amber pixel eyes follow the printing boundary; no face UI outside its black lens. Physically buildable, precise world scale, rich high-end cinematic material rendering. No panel labels, no arrows, no typography, no UI. One complete object image.

entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a beautiful four-panel 2x2 character-mechanism sheet of the SAME spherical ivory AI head from this reference, with correct metal camera iris, gold gimbal neck, side ruby bearing and separate underside optical pickup emitter. These are close-up renderings of one physically modelable 3D machine, all identical shell construction/materials. Atomic Heart retrofuturist industrial design, refined champagne gold and glazed ivory, black glass and amber pixel matrix; uncanny intelligent personality, not children's toy or a emoji cartoon. Charcoal studio background. Small panel labels only: "WATCH", "CURIOUS", "PROUD", "SLEEP".

WATCH: iris fully open, two slim rectangular amber pixel eyes looking slightly sideways in ONE black circular lens; head upright, emitter dark. Shell mechanical seams, eight overlapping matte-metal iris blades retracted into a gold camera ring; pixel face is a flat/curved matrix INSIDE the real lens, no floating display.

CURIOUS: head tilts twelve degrees at actual side pitch/yaw gimbal, shutter closes modestly to tighten the pupil, amber pixel eyebrows/eyes become one raised and one narrowed. Clearly display limited deliberate physical motion and a glancing eye direction. The underside projector remains independently upright, not tilted with the face.

PROUD: after successfully printing a specimen, the camera shutter performs a playful asymmetric-looking wink via the inner matrix; two angular happy eye arcs on amber matrix, aperture momentarily partly closing. NO mouth, hearts, floating symbols or decorative particle confetti. Personality through subtle timing and eye shape.

SLEEP: same head bowed just a little at the gimbal, real spiral camera-iris blades almost fully CLOSED, leave only a tiny center slit and dim amber line visible behind it. The photon emitter fully dark. No black panel painted to fake closure: show actual overlapping metal blade surfaces and mechanical aperture near shut. A tiny warm standby diode on the side.

Show enough of the mounting neck/first link in each close-up to make attachment and construction clear, but do not show the base or records. Professional cinematic hard-surface finish: broad gold reflections, satin machined dark shutter blades, smoke-glass depth, ivory has ceramic glaze not woven/cloth/plastic. No numbers, arrows, extra limbs, claws or speech bubbles. The eye matrix is a deliberate coarse approximately 24x24 amber micro-LED array visible at close range. Exact same identity in all four panels.

entries.prompt:
Production texture asset, not concept art and not a scene. Create a square 2x2 atlas of FOUR emission masks, each exactly equal size and separated ONLY by pure black gutters. Pure black opaque background, monochrome white intensity with subtle gray variation, no labels, no borders, no lighting render, no objects, no text, no color. Fine crisp elegant optical-engineering detail. The masks will be wrapped on actual 3D surfaces of an Atomic Heart style AI robot's tractor beam and record printer, not displayed as an entire flat image.

Top left cell: a straight UV-unwrapped structured-light field curtain. Roughly 24 very fine vertical strands running within the center 80 percent of the tile from top to bottom, with a few slender crossing horizontal dashed timing bands. Thread intensities varied, some broken micro-gaps, overall transparent black negative space. Soft fade within last 8 percent near all tile edges. NO drawn cone or perspective: straight rectangular unwrapped texture only.

Top right cell: concentric precision interference traces on a disc, centered perfectly in its tile. Very fine interrupted concentric circles, six discrete radial feeder sectors, sparse luminous contact nodes, some short technical line segments. No fantasy symbols, no text, no filled disk. Ring outer diameter 75 percent of tile, black center small aperture. Sophisticated schematic reticle that can rotate over actual black vinyl.

Bottom left cell: close network of luminous capillary microfilaments branching upward. Main thin paths rise from six bottom roots, branch into small crisp hooked strands in the upper two-thirds, a few tiny nodes at junctions. On black, generous empty space. No thick lightning strokes, no soft smoke. This mask modulates real 3D lines feeding specimen assembly points.

Bottom right cell: one tiny isolated elegant optical hot point exactly centered, with a very small white core, short sharp horizontal and vertical diffraction needles and only a restrained close halo fading to pure black well before tile edges. It will be instanced as microscopic material grains, not big stars. No scattered multiple stars.

Uniform pure black gutters 4 percent of image width on all outer margins and between tiles; no texture crossing a tile boundary. Asset-only technical mask sheet with subtle beautiful density, high resolution.
